title: Tracing a strict specialization by a DVR
statement: Let X be a locally noetherian scheme and y specialize to x with y distinct from x. There exist a discrete valuation ring R and a scheme morphism a:Spec R→X taking its closed point to x and its zero prime to y.

proof.text: Choose an affine chart j:Spec B→X containing x. Its open image also contains y. Since j is an embedding, the lifted points y₀ and x₀ specialize in Spec B; their ideals form a strict inclusion. The ring B is noetherian because X is locally noetherian.

Apply the proved library theorem Ideal.exists_isDiscreteValuationRing_of_lt to that strict inclusion. Its map φ:B→R has kernel the smaller prime and inverse image of the maximal ideal equal to the larger prime. Compose Spec.map φ with j and compute both point images by PrimeSpectrum.ext.

theorem exists_trait_of_strict_specializes {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    {x y : X} (hxy : y ⤳ x) (hne : y ≠ x) :
    ∃ (R : Type u) (_ : CommRing R) (_ : IsDomain R) (_ : IsDiscreteValuationRing R)
      (a : Spec (.of R) ⟶ X),
      a (closedPoint R) = x ∧ a (⟨⊥, Ideal.isPrime_bot⟩ : PrimeSpectrum R) = y
